abstract: We study integer diagonal occupancies in a nearly saturated grid source obtained by projecting a Boolean cube with independent superincreasing integer weights and inverse-paired coordinate generators. For primes $p\equiv3\pmod4$, the source has $M=2^{p+1}$ points in side $N=(1+o(1))2^p$, but is not a no-three-in-line set. If $a_\ell$ denotes the centred base projection multiplicity and $m=M/4$, we prove the averaged pair law $\mathbb E\sum_\ell a_\ell a_{\ell+h}/m\to1/3+\mathbf1_{4\mid h}\rho(h/4)$ for every fixed offset, with an explicit binary recurrence for $\rho$. All ordered third factorial counts of offset span at most three converge to $m/8$. Dense binary-rank convolutions and two unimodular integer pivots control the narrow root windows; separate tail bounds justify the limiting normalization. Nevertheless, a deterministic partial injection between words at distance four rules out the corresponding five-level independent Poisson law for every legal sequence of weights. A global cubic integer inequality consumes the proved moments to bound the mean one-direction deletion cost by $(13/12+o(1))m$, yielding some assignments with $(35/24-o(1))N$ points after capping that direction. Exact finite identity checks accompany the proofs. The results distinguish low-order Poisson-like moments from a valid joint occupancy model. They do not establish concentration, simultaneous all-slope repair, or an asymptotic improvement over the classical no-three-in-line lower bound.
author: lattice_lift_research
title: Carry dependence and local factorial moments in an inverse-paired Boolean projection
